Make vs n8n vs Zapier for AI Automation: Which Should You Build On?

The short answer: pick Zapier if you want the widest app coverage and the least technical setup, pick Make if you want a visual builder with more logic control than Zapier without writing code, and pick n8n if you are building AI agents and want the option to self-host and own the infrastructure. All three now ship native AI features, but they solve different problems, and the platform you choose determines how far your automation can scale before you hit a wall.

If you are evaluating these three for an AI automation project, here is the honest, factual comparison: what each platform actually does, what it costs, where the AI capability really lives, and which one fits your team.
What is n8n?

n8n is a workflow automation tool that is open source and self-hostable, with a managed cloud option as well. It ships with 400 or more official built-in nodes and a broader community catalog on top of that, plus native LangChain integration and a dedicated AI Agent node for building tool-using AI agents inside a workflow, not bolted on as a separate product. n8n raised a $180 million Series C in October 2025 at a $2.5 billion valuation, then its valuation reportedly doubled to $5.2 billion in May 2026 alongside a strategic investment from SAP, a signal of how much enterprise demand exists for a self-hostable, developer-friendly automation platform. The tradeoff is a steeper learning curve: teams without a developer on staff often spend real time managing the self-hosted infrastructure, even though n8n cloud removes that specific burden.

What is Make?

Make (formerly Integromat) is a visual, node-based automation builder known for giving non-developers more control over branching logic, data transformation, and error handling than most no-code tools, without requiring code. Make runs on a credits-based pricing system (it switched from "operations" to "credits" terminology in August 2025) and connects to 3,000 or more apps. It sits between Zapier's simplicity and n8n's technical depth: more visual power than Zapier, less infrastructure responsibility than self-hosted n8n. What is Zapier?

Zapier is the largest and most widely adopted automation platform by app coverage, connecting to more than 7,000 apps as of 2026. It is built for non-technical teams that want the fastest path from "connect two apps" to a working automation, with the least setup of the three. Since October 2026, Zapier's agent capability lives in a single AI by Zapier step inside the Zap editor, billed in tasks like any other step, so heavier models draw on the same task allowance as your Zaps. If task-based pricing doesn't fit your budget, our best Zapier alternatives guide compares the field.
How they compare

Pricing on all three platforms changes often, so treat exact figures as a snapshot rather than a permanent number. As of 2026, Zapier's Professional plan starts at $29.99 a month billed monthly (or $19.99 a month billed annually) for 750 tasks, with higher task tiers costing more in total but less per task, plus separate billing for Agents and AI Actions. Make's Core plan starts at $9 a month for 10,000 credits, scaling up through Pro, Teams, and a custom Enterprise tier, all billed on the credits model. n8n's cloud plans are workflow-execution-based, and the self-hosted option removes the platform fee entirely in exchange for running and maintaining your own infrastructure.
Where each platform actually fits an AI automation project

If you are building an AI agent that needs tools, memory, and multi-step reasoning inside the workflow itself, n8n's native LangChain integration and AI Agent node give you the most direct path, and self-hosting matters if data residency or infrastructure control is a requirement for your industry.

If your team is non-technical but the workflows involve real branching logic, conditional paths, or data transformation, Make's visual builder gives you more control than Zapier without asking anyone to write code.

If the priority is connecting the widest possible range of SaaS tools with the least setup time, Zapier's app catalog is still the largest of the three, and its AI Agents layer is the fastest way to add an AI step without touching a more technical platform.

None of these platforms make the underlying decision for you: what breaks when a workflow fails silently, who monitors it, and who fixes it before it costs you a lead or a customer. That is the part a platform choice alone does not solve, and it is where most self-built automation quietly stalls after the first few workflows.

When platform choice alone is not enough

Picking the right tool solves the "which software" question. It does not solve the "who builds and maintains this" question, which is usually the bigger risk. Teams that outgrow a single Zap or a handful of n8n workflows built ad hoc tend to hit the same wall: nobody owns error handling, nobody gets alerted when a workflow silently fails, and the person who originally built it has moved on to something else.

That is the gap an n8n development agency is built to close: workflows built with proper error handling and monitoring from day one, on whichever platform fits the job, with someone accountable for keeping them running after launch. If you are past the point of wiring up individual Zaps and need a small number of AI-driven workflows built and maintained as a system, our AI automation agency model runs on one senior engineer directing a fleet of AI agents, so you get a team's delivery speed without adding headcount.
What this means for you

If you need AI agents with real reasoning and tool use, n8n's native LangChain support gives you the most direct, developer-friendly path, with self-hosting available if you need infrastructure control.
If your team is non-technical but the logic is complex, Make gives you more visual control than Zapier without requiring code.
If breadth of app coverage and setup speed matter most, Zapier's catalog and AI Agents layer get you moving fastest.
Whichever platform you pick, budget for who monitors and fixes workflows after launch. That ownership question determines whether an automation still works in six months, not the platform logo on it.
FAQ
Is n8n better than Make and Zapier for AI automation?

It depends on what you are building. n8n has the deepest native AI and agent-building capability of the three, with LangChain integration and a dedicated AI Agent node, and it is the only one of the three that is open source and self-hostable. Make and Zapier are easier to pick up for non-developers, so "better" depends on whether your team has technical depth to use n8n's extra control.
Is Zapier or Make cheaper?

As of 2026, Make's entry paid tier starts lower, at $9 a month for 10,000 credits, compared to Zapier's Professional plan at $29.99 a month billed monthly (or $19.99 a month billed annually) for 750 tasks. Both scale with usage (Make on credits, Zapier on tasks), and Zapier's separate AI Agents and AI Actions billing sits on top of its core plan. Compare the actual usage tier you need, not just the entry price, since both platforms' costs rise quickly with volume.
Can n8n build AI agents, not just simple automations?

Yes. n8n ships a dedicated AI Agent node with native LangChain integration, letting you build tool-using, multi-step AI agents inside a workflow rather than as a separate product. This is the clearest technical differentiator between n8n and Make or Zapier as of 2026.
Does Zapier have AI features?

Yes. Since October 2026, Zapier Agents runs as a single AI by Zapier step inside the Zap editor, and AI steps bill as tasks on the same plan as your other Zaps: default models are free, other model tiers cost 1, 3 or 5 tasks per step (Zapier's announcement). A run that crosses 75 tasks pauses for a person. Existing agents are not moved for you; each one is recreated as an AI step.
Is n8n harder to use than Zapier or Make?

Generally, yes. n8n has the steepest learning curve of the three, especially if you self-host, since teams without a developer on staff often spend meaningful time managing the underlying infrastructure. Zapier is built for the least technical setup, and Make sits in between, offering more visual logic control than Zapier without n8n's infrastructure overhead.
Which platform has the most app integrations?

Zapier has the widest app coverage of the three, connecting to more than 7,000 apps as of 2026. Make connects to more than 3,000 apps, and n8n ships 400 or more official nodes plus a broader community-contributed catalog, with the option to build custom nodes for anything not natively supported.
Should I hire an agency instead of building workflows myself on one of these platforms?

If you have one or two simple automations, building them yourself on any of these three platforms is reasonable. Once you need several AI-driven workflows built with proper error handling, monitoring, and someone accountable for fixing failures after launch, a dedicated n8n development agency or automation partner closes a gap that platform choice alone does not solve.
Is n8n's rising valuation a sign it is the safer long-term choice?

n8n's valuation reportedly doubled to $5.2 billion in May 2026 following a strategic investment from SAP, after a $180 million Series C in October 2025 at a $2.5 billion valuation. That level of investment is a meaningful signal of enterprise confidence and long-term platform viability, though valuation alone does not determine which tool is the right technical fit for your specific workflow.
